title: Operational guide to transfer resolution
summary: The Bank of England has published an operational guide describing how it would execute transfer resolution actions for failing financial institutions, covering transfers to private sector purchasers (PSP) and bridge banks. The guide provides transparency on the Bank's resolution powers and operational processes, including stylised timelines, auction and bidder selection approaches, and governance structures for bridge bank transfers.
key_points: Transfer resolution involves transferring shares or business of a failed firm to a PSP, bridge bank, or asset management vehicle using Bank's stabilisation powers
Transfer to a PSP allows transfer of all or part of a firm's business to a willing, authorised buyer without consent of the failed firm, shareholders, customers or counterparties
Bridge bank transfers temporarily hold business in a Bank-controlled company to maintain critical functions until sale or orderly wind-down
Bank Resolution (Recapitalisation) Act 2025 (BRRA 2025) introduced a recapitalisation payment mechanism
Annex 1 contains two historical examples: Dunfermline Building Society (2009) transfer to Nationwide, and SVBUK (2023) mandatory reduction and share transfer to HSBC UK
HM Treasury has sole responsibility for authorising use of any stabilisation power with implications for public funds
why_it_matters: This guide provides operational transparency on UK bank resolution procedures. It affects firms near resolution thresholds, shareholders and capital instrument holders who may face losses, and market participants involved in execution of transfers. While this is a procedural/operational document rather than a market-moving catalyst, it increases understanding of how authorities would handle a failing financial institution.
macro_context: Resolution regime guidance is relevant to financial stability but is not a macro catalyst in the traditional sense (rate decisions, economic data releases, etc.). This document does not itself move markets; it describes operational procedures for handling failing institutions.
market_structure_context: This guide is directly relevant to the pricing of UK bank capital instruments. It clarifies that in a transfer resolution, shareholders and holders of regulatory capital instruments (AT1, Tier 2, and other non-excluded liabilities) may be subject to losses. The inclusion of historical precedents (Dunfermline 2009, SVBUK 2023) and the description of the Bank Resolution (Recapitalisation) Act 2025 recapitalisation payment mechanism informs how investors should model resolution risk in UK bank securities. Participants holding AT1 or Tier 2 instruments in UK banks near resolution thresholds should treat this as reference material for loss-at-resolution scenarios.
